raw_segments.text: a splendid midsummer shone over England, skies so pure, suns so radiant as were then seen in
long succession, seldom favor even singly, our wavegirt land. It was as if a band of Italian
days had come from the south, like a flock of glorious passenger birds, and lighted to rest
them on the cliffs of Albion. The hay was all got in, the fields round Thornfield were green and
shorn, the roads white and baked, the trees were in their dark prime. Hedge and wood,
full-leaved and deeply tinted, contrasted well with the sunny hue of the cleared meadows between.
